content: Carboxypeptidase N catalytic chain is an enzyme in humans that is encoded by the CPN1 gene. Carboxypeptidase N is a plasma metallo-protease that specifically cleaves basic amino acids from the C-terminal end of peptides and proteins. This enzyme plays a critical role in regulating peptides such as kinins and anaphylatoxins. It is also referred to as kininase-1 and an anaphylatoxin inactivator due to its functional properties. The enzyme exists as a tetramer, consisting of two identical regulatory subunits and two identical catalytic subunits. The CPN1 gene encodes the catalytic subunit of this tetramer. Mutations in the CPN1 gene can lead to conditions such as angioedema or chronic urticaria, which are associated with carboxypeptidase N deficiency. In melanocytic cells, the expression of the CPN1 gene may be regulated by the transcription factor MITF.
